newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines, Moslem rebels adjourn talks.
newsitem.headline: Philippines, Moslem rebels adjourn talks.

text.p: A Philippine government panel and Moslem rebels have adjourned peace talks but plan next month to resume negotiations on ending fighting in the south, officials said on Wednesday.

The two sides, which met in southern Sultan Kudarat town on Tuesday, cancelled a scheduled meeting of their technical committees on Wednesday and instead issued a joint statement saying they needed more time to study each other's proposals, including a ceasefire in the southern Mindanao region.

The talks were between a government panel headed by retired army chief Fortunato Abat and representatives of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), which is fighting for an Islamic state in Mindanao.
The MILF is the second Moslem rebel group with whom Manila is trying to conclude a peace deal.
President Fidel Ramos's government in October signed a peace accord with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) ending a 24-year MNLF-led revolt for Moslem autonomy.

The military considers the MILF a more hardline group because of its insistence on a separate Moslem state in Mindanao, where the bulk of the largely Christian country's five million Moslem minority live.
The joint statement described the preliminary talks between the government and the MILF as "a step towards the attainment of a just and lasting peace in Mindanao."
It said the two sides exchanged various proposals, including guidelines for a ceasefire as well as an agenda for formal talks to be held later.

The statement gave no details but MILF officers said their ceasefire proposal called for government recognition of "MILF-controlled areas," the pull-out of military troops in such areas and a ban on the future entry of soldiers to those areas.
There was no immediate reaction from the government on this.
The two sides are to meet again on February 25-26 in Sultan Kudarat, Maguindanao province, 800 km (500 miles) south of Manila.
Another rebel faction, the fundamentalist Abu Sayyaf group, has shunned talks with Manila. The military has blamed it for bombings, kidnappings and raids on Christian towns in the past three years.
The military estimates MILF strength at between 6,000 and 8,000 men and that of the Abu Sayyaf at several hundred. The MILF says it has 80,000 fighters.
